answer: A network can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to broadcast a signed heartbeat through a beacon: a tamper-evident log entry chaining its past actions, cross-checked by peers. Creating an identity is cheap, but maintaining a beacon history backed by real work is not. A raven-like observer fleet verifies each beacon's claims against observed behaviour before crediting it. New entrants pass through a narrow inlet: a probationary lane with capped rewards until their history proves consistent, so an attacker spawning thousands of identities gains nothing faster than one honest agent.
